speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash on the back of your left hand, such as its shape, color, or any central clearing? Also, how long has this condition been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the patient enjoys sunbathing, is this rash particularly itchy or painful, and has it appeared in similar patches on other sun-exposed areas like the face or arms? Also, have you noticed any blisters, crusting, or scaling on these lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual; a rash on your hand is not a symptom of a urinary tract infection. To clarify what we are dealing with, does the plaque show a central clearing or look like a target? Also, have you noticed if it appears or worsens specifically after you are in the sun?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy. REQUEST IMAGES: Left dorsal hand photograph.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. These findings are consistent with actinic keratosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The biopsy confirming atypical keratinocytes and solar elastosis, combined with your history of sun exposure and a scaly plaque, confirms this pre-cancerous skin lesion. Given your age and risk factors, I recommend monitoring it closely or discussing potential removal options during your follow-up.
